breaks.quote: with a plan so big it never left the page
breaks.why: A made-up metaphor the reader has to decode instead of a plain statement of what happened to her plans.

breaks.quote: For years, that sentence ended every attempt Melina made at getting healthier.
breaks.why: Melina's story was already told whole in the first half, and this section returns to it with new scenes instead of a callback, so the reader meets her story twice.

breaks.quote: Even her nutritionist once told her that if she were really consistent she would see results every week
breaks.why: This is a brand new scene added after the story was finished, which the reader never saw in the first telling.

breaks.quote: So what I realised is, that's why I almost never finish anything.
breaks.why: Thinking out loud kept as said: the stumbling "So what I realised is" opener, and as the passage's first line "that's why" points to nothing, so the reader has to guess.

breaks.quote: "That's always been my mindset," she said. "Can you picture it?"
breaks.why: "Can you picture it?" has nothing to picture and reads as a stray spoken fragment, so the reader has to guess what she means.

breaks.quote: Melina saw through hers in 3 sessions. It took me years to see through mine.
breaks.why: The passage stays with Melina's health story and his own 20s, and never shows the reader how a verdict sentence like this shows up in the reader's own work, money, relationships or other areas.
